chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban al-Ahmar from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The wearing of silk and brocade is not permissible (for men), so as for selling them, there is no problem.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for men to wear silk and brocade according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the distinction between the prohibition of wearing silk and brocade (al-dibaj) for men and the permissibility of their trade, reflecting the juristic consensus that the impurity lies in the act of adornment rather than the commodity itself. It highlights the practical application of fiqh in daily commerce and dress, a key topic in Shia legal tradition where the ruling is specific to the male gender unless otherwise specified by context.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Al Ahmar, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It is not correct wearing the silk and the brocade (for men), so as for selling these, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 7. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban al- Ahmar from Muhammad ibn Musiim who has said the folio wing: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Silk garments are not proper, however, selling such garments is not unlawful.’”
